location: prop:exp:share: "after the sharing pass the cluster of $T_l$ is $C^+=D\cap\inst(T_l)$, in any order; and $\Acc(C^+)\subseteq\inst(T_l)$, with equality whenever $C^+$ contains an anchor"; proof: "Let $C'$ be the growing cluster, initially the phase-one cluster $C$ with $l(C)=l$"; E3 Reading "as \cref{prop:exp:share} predicts"
problem: The proof only shows that each phase-1 cluster C grows to D∩inst(T_{l(C)}). It never shows that every target labels a phase-1 cluster, and in fact one need not. Counterexample, computed with the implementation (research/paper-review/scratch/share_cex.py): targets U_add0=(z+0=z), U_0add=(0+z=z) and T3=(1+z=Sz), all valid; data D={0+0=0, 0+2=2, 1+0=1, 1+1=2}. Every set lying in no single instance set contains a cross pair whose minimal template is false (z+z=w; z0+z1=Sz2; z0+Sz1=2), so (S+) holds even for an ideal refuter. Phase 1, merging the largest common prefix first, builds {1+0=1, 1+1=2} (lies only in inst(T3)) and {0+0=0, 0+2=2} (lies only in inst(U_0add)), so (P) holds. The sharing pass adds nothing. U_add0 owns no cluster, and DTRC+share rejects 2+0=2 and 3+0=3. The membership-labelled tagged learner sees {0+0=0, 1+0=1}, an anchor with Min={z+0=z}, and is exact. So the claim "the cluster of T_l is C+ … with equality whenever C+ contains an anchor" is false for this T_l. So is the record's claim that DTRC+share is exact whenever the membership-labelled learner is, even for anchor-based exactness. Nested targets (U_add00 ⊆ U_add0 in E4(a)) also own no cluster.
fix: Replace the conclusion by: "Then distinct phase-1 clusters have distinct labels; after the sharing pass each phase-1 cluster $C$, with $l:=l(C)$, has become $C^+=D\cap\inst(T_l)$, in any order; and $\Acc(C^+)\subseteq\inst(T_l)$, with equality whenever $C^+$ contains an anchor of $T_l$. Under \textup{(H-ref)} $\Acc(C^+)$ is the acceptance set of the tagged learner with membership labels for $T_l$. A target that labels no phase-1 cluster gets no cluster of its own and may be learned incompletely even when its membership-labelled data contain an anchor." In the proof, write "For each phase-1 cluster $C$, with $l:=l(C)$, let $C'$ be the growing cluster, initially $C$." After the proof, add the counterexample: targets $z+0=z$, $0+z=z$, $1+z=Sz$; data $\{0+0=0,0+2=2,1+0=1,1+1=2\}$; $2+0=2$ is rejected. In E3's Reading, replace "as \cref{prop:exp:share} predicts" by "consistent with \cref{prop:exp:share} (here every target with data labels a phase-1 cluster)".

location: paragraph "E6 and E7": "$k=9$ accepts $0/8$ from two induction instances (the spare slot keeps them apart) and $8/8$ from three. No false non-instance was accepted. This reproduces the prior untagged result (\cref{sec:many})"
problem: One of the two three-instance runs (e6_kunion.md) uses the motives x=x, ¬x=0, x+0=x. Its split {Ind(x=x), Ind(x+0=x)} | {Ind(¬x=0)} has a root-homogeneous block, which is not a DT° anchor (anchor theorem (R)+(N); §6 slot accounting). I computed (scratch/e6_dtf_vs_dt.py) that the DT° template (f(0)=0 ∧ ∀x(f(x)=x→f(Sx)=Sx))→∀x f(x)=x covers both data, has only true instances (so it avoids every sound negative), and misses the query Ind(x·0=0). Hence DT° at k=9, and the prior and §6 theory, predict rejection. In DT°_F the pair has Min = {T_Ind, (f0=0∧∀x(P(x)→P(Sx)))→∀xP(x)}; the second is refuted. So 8/8 arises only because f(x) ∉ DT°_F, and only relative to the negatives. The run whose third motive is ∃y.x<y does agree with the theory.
fix: Replace the last two sentences by: "… and $8/8$ from three. With third motive $\exists y\,x<y$ this agrees with the slot accounting of \cref{sec:many} (every 2-block split has an anchor block). With third motive $x+0=x$ it does not: $\{\Ind(x=x),\Ind(x+0=x)\}$ is root-homogeneous, and the $\DT$ template $(f(0)=0\wedge\forall x(f(x)=x\to f(Sx)=Sx))\to\forall x\,f(x)=x$ covers it, has only true instances, and misses held-out queries such as $\Ind(x\cdot0=0)$. $\DTF$ lacks this template, so here the implemented class accepts more than $\DT$ would. No false non-instance was accepted. The other rows reproduce the prior untagged result \src{experiments E6; prior pa-untagged}."
